subquestions.text_open:
3.3 Changing the metal species in the tetragonal crystal above and introducing a slight distortion gives a monoclinic crystal. Its projection along the $b$ direction is shown below, with black spheres representing chromium atoms, gray spheres representing manganese atoms, and white spheres representing phosphorus atoms.
3.3.1 Give the chemical formula of this crystal.

text_images.description: Projection of the monoclinic crystal along the $b$ direction. The main drawing is enclosed by a thin solid black, inclined parallelepiped wireframe representing the unit-cell boundary. Its bottom edge is horizontal, and its inclined edges run from upper left to lower right with a slope of approximately -1. The bottom edge is approximately equal in length to its corresponding height. The positive $c$ direction runs from left to right, while the positive $a$ direction runs from lower right to upper left along an inclined edge. The drawing contains 12 solid black spheres representing chromium atoms, 12 gray spheres representing manganese atoms, and 8 white spheres representing phosphorus atoms. Short line segments connect the spheres into a network.
